text: Prior work on the psychological drivers of misinformation belief indicates that individuals' resistance to correcting false beliefs is shaped by motivated reasoning and prior attitudes, which is relevant to H2 (attitudes toward AI) and H4 (trust in online information) (Ecker et al., 2022). A review of disinformation in social media highlights the growing difficulty of distinguishing authentic from fabricated content online, providing context for H1, H5, and H6 [citation removed: not in retrieved set]. In the educational domain, the rapid adoption of generative AI has prompted concern about its effects on assessment integrity and student attitudes, offering a partial analogue for H2 (Rudolph et al., 2023). However, none of the retrieved works directly examines whether specific interventions shift AI-detection accuracy, confidence in detection, or recognition of authentic posts, leaving H1, H3, H5, and H6 largely unaddressed in this set.
